Definition: first person plural indicative of G1510; we are:--are, be, have our being, X have hope, + (the gospel) was (preached unto) us.
BiblicalUsage: Esmén is the word for 'we are' — the first-person plural of the verb to be. It is the word of belonging: 'we are the children of God', 'we are witnesses'. The form itself is a confession of who we are together.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that esmén matters because it is never singular: it is the word the church uses about itself, together.
